Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co Announces New Chief Operating Officer

Amman – Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, one of the nation’s leading energy companies, has announced the appointment of Eng. Firas Al-Khatib as the company’s new Chief Operating Officer (COO), effective next month. The appointment comes as the company advances its strategic plans to expand refining capacity and enhance operational efficiency.

Al-Khatib, who brings over two decades of experience in the oil and gas sector, will be responsible for overseeing the company’s core refining operations in Zarqa, as well as spearheading ongoing modernization projects. He joins Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co from a senior leadership role at Eastern Horizons Energy, where he managed large-scale infrastructure projects in the region.

“We are delighted to welcome Eng. Al-Khatib to our executive team,” said Samir Al-Tarawneh, Chairman of the Board at Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co. “His extensive expertise in refinery operations and project management will further strengthen our company as we enter a new phase of growth.”

The appointment is seen by industry analysts as a move to support the company’s recently announced JD 2 billion expansion plan, which aims to increase refining capacity to over 120,000 barrels per day by 2026. The expansion is expected to boost local fuel production, reduce reliance on imported refined products, and create hundreds of new jobs, particularly in Zarqa and surrounding areas.

Local energy market observers have welcomed the news. “Eng. Al-Khatib is known for his hands-on leadership style and his deep technical knowledge,” said Rania Haddad, senior analyst at the Jordan Energy Forum. “His appointment signals the company’s commitment to operational excellence at a critical time for Jordan’s energy sector.”

In a brief statement, Al-Khatib expressed gratitude for the opportunity and outlined his vision for the role. “It is an honour to join Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co at such a pivotal moment,” he said. “I look forward to working with our talented team to deliver on our ambitious plans and to ensure we continue to meet the Kingdom’s energy needs safely and efficiently.”

The Jordanian General Trade Union for Oil and Chemical Workers also welcomed the appointment, noting Al-Khatib’s history of productive engagement with labour groups. “We look forward to fruitful cooperation and continued dialogue under his leadership,” the union said in a statement on Thursday.

Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co is expected to provide further details on its operational roadmap following Al-Khatib’s official start date next month.
